claims.text: The manual's storage precautions apply when a motorcycle will not be used for a month or more, and for re-use after storage it says it is preferable to have the motorcycle prepared through a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre so it is restored to its peak operating condition.
The battery is the main concern. If the motorcycle is used very rarely and the terminals are not disconnected, the battery is bound to lose its charge and can end up dead.

For storage of a month or longer, the manual advises disconnecting the battery terminals and removing the battery. Before refitting it, check that the battery voltage is within specification. If it is not, recharge it from an authorised service workshop or battery dealer.
For checking battery voltage, the manual says to contact a Royal Enfield Authorised Service Centre or a battery service centre.

If the bike was prepared with the manual's storage steps, those steps included draining the fuel from the tank and induction system and removing the charging circuit fuse from the fuse box. Anything done this way is part of the bike's stored state before you start it.

This partly answers your question. The retrieved manual information does not establish that a bike stored for over a month can simply be restarted without preparation, and it gives no step-by-step restart procedure for a bike coming out of storage. It also does not give the battery voltage specification or say how to check it yourself.

unanswered_parts: Whether a bike stored over a month can be restarted without any preparation
A restart-from-storage procedure and the battery voltage specification
